"""Light monitoring (SPEC §7), with APScheduler.

- Every 15 minutes: site points + opens over HTTPS.
- Daily: the same, plus email settings and "settings unchanged since launch", and
  days left on the certificate and domain.
- A failure is re-checked once a minute later (rule out blips). If it still fails,
  the Doctor explains and applies a safe playbook fix; anything still broken is
  emailed to the owner's PERSONAL email (once per problem until it passes again).
- Domain expiry warnings at 30 / 7 / 1 days (renewal costs money: alert only).
  Certificate warnings at 7 / 1 days (Caddy renews certificates by itself well before that).
- Practice businesses use the fake world, so their "emails" never leave the server.

Switch off with MONITOR_ENABLED=false. Tests never start the scheduler; they call
the job methods directly.
"""

import json
from collections.abc import Callable
from datetime import timedelta

from apscheduler.schedulers.background import BackgroundScheduler
from sqlalchemy.engine import Engine
from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app import audit, renewals
from app.agents.claude_client import Claude
from app.agents.launch_check import AlreadyChecking, NotLaunched, latest_launched_plan, run_checks
from app.config import Settings
from app.integrations import Integrations
from app.models import Alert, Business, CheckRun, utcnow
from app.safety.access import owner_emails

QUICK_MINUTES = 15
RECHECK_SECONDS = 60
SHOP_BUDGET = {"quick": 90, "daily": 300, "recheck": 300}  # seconds one shop may take in a round
FLAP_WINDOW = timedelta(days=1)
QUICK_CHECKS = ["site_points", "https"]
EMAIL_CHECKS = ["email_mx", "email_spf", "email_dkim", "email_dmarc"]  # read-only on shops under the app's domain
DOMAIN_WARN_DAYS = renewals.THRESHOLDS  # one set for everything a person renews (S10)
CERT_WARN_DAYS = renewals.CERT_THRESHOLDS


def daily_checks(mode: str) -> list[str]:
    # The daily test order carries a fresh code. For an inbox we can't read it proves "form accepted ->
    # mail server accepted" only (the report says so); delivery needs the owner's tap on that email.
    return QUICK_CHECKS + EMAIL_CHECKS + ["settings_match", "test_order"]


def proof_aware(when):
    """SQLite hands datetimes back without a timezone; ours are always UTC."""
    return when if when.tzinfo is not None else when.replace(tzinfo=utcnow().tzinfo)


class Monitor:
    def __init__(self, engine: Engine, settings: Settings, integ_for: Callable[[Business], Integrations],
                 claude: Claude, scheduler: BackgroundScheduler | None = None, team: Integrations | None = None):
        self.engine, self.settings, self.integ_for, self.claude = engine, settings, integ_for, claude
        self.team = team  # the server's own integrations: the app domain, the team mailbox, the app zone
        self.scheduler = scheduler or BackgroundScheduler(timezone="UTC")

    # ---------- scheduler wiring ----------

    def register(self) -> None:
        self.scheduler.add_job(self.run_quick, "interval", minutes=QUICK_MINUTES, id="monitor_quick",
                               replace_existing=True, max_instances=1, coalesce=True)
        self.scheduler.add_job(self.run_daily, "interval", days=1, id="monitor_daily",
                               replace_existing=True, max_instances=1, coalesce=True)
        if self.team is not None:
            self.scheduler.add_job(self.watch_addresses, "interval", days=1, id="watch_addresses",
                                   replace_existing=True, max_instances=1, coalesce=True)
            self.scheduler.add_job(self.team_renewals, "interval", days=1, id="team_renewals",
                                   replace_existing=True, max_instances=1, coalesce=True)
            self.scheduler.add_job(self.zone_hygiene, "interval", days=1, id="zone_hygiene",
                                   replace_existing=True, max_instances=1, coalesce=True)

    def start(self) -> None:
        self.register()
        self.scheduler.start()

    def shutdown(self) -> None:
        if self.scheduler.running:
            self.scheduler.shutdown(wait=False)

    def schedule_recheck(self, business_id: int, names: list[str]) -> None:
        self.scheduler.add_job(self.recheck, "date", run_date=utcnow() + timedelta(seconds=RECHECK_SECONDS),
                               args=[business_id, names], id=f"recheck-{business_id}", replace_existing=True)

    # ---------- jobs ----------

    def live_business_ids(self) -> list[int]:
        """Shops to watch: live, not paused. Guest practice shops are short-lived and aren't watched."""
        with Session(self.engine) as s:
            return list(s.exec(select(Business.id).where(Business.status == "live", Business.paused == False,  # noqa: E712
                                                         Business.guest_hash == "")).all())

    def run_quick(self) -> None:
        self._round("quick")

    def run_daily(self) -> None:
        self._round("daily")

    def _round(self, kind: str) -> None:
        """Every live shop, one after the other. A shop whose check blows up is recorded as "couldn't finish"
        (never as passed) and the round carries on with the next shop."""
        for bid in self.live_business_ids():
            try:
                self.check_business(bid, kind)
            except Exception as e:
                with Session(self.engine) as s:
                    audit.record(s, actor="monitor", action="monitor_shop", target=f"business:{bid}", result="failed",
                                 business_id=bid, detail=f"{kind} check couldn't finish: {type(e).__name__}")

    def _context(self, business_id: int):
        with Session(self.engine) as s:
            b = s.get(Business, business_id)
            plan = latest_launched_plan(s, business_id) if b else None
            if b is None or plan is None:
                return None
            s.expunge_all()
            return b, plan

    def check_business(self, business_id: int, kind: str) -> list[str]:
        """Run the quick or daily checks without fixing. Returns the failing check names."""
        found = self._context(business_id)
        if found is None:
            return []
        b, plan = found
        names = QUICK_CHECKS if kind == "quick" else daily_checks(plan.mode)
        try:
            summary = run_checks(self.engine, self.settings, self.integ_for(b), self.claude, plan.id,
                                 trigger=f"monitor_{kind}", names=names, fix=False,
                                 budget_seconds=SHOP_BUDGET[kind])
        except (NotLaunched, AlreadyChecking):  # e.g. the owner just pressed "Run checks now": skip this round
            return []
        # "couldn't finish" / "our lookup failed" is not a failure of the shop: no re-check as one, no alert,
        # and it doesn't clear an open alert either (we simply don't know)
        failing = [f.check for f in summary.failed if not f.unfinished]
        if failing:
            self.schedule_recheck(business_id, failing)
        self.resolve(business_id, [n for n in names if n not in {f.check for f in summary.failed}])
        if kind == "daily":
            self.expiry_alerts(business_id, summary.run_id)
        return failing

    def recheck(self, business_id: int, names: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        """A minute later: re-check; the Doctor fixes what it safely can; alert on what's left."""
        found = self._context(business_id)
        if found is None:
            return []
        b, plan = found
        try:
            summary = run_checks(self.engine, self.settings, self.integ_for(b), self.claude, plan.id,
                                 trigger="monitor_recheck", names=names, fix=True,
                                 budget_seconds=SHOP_BUDGET["recheck"])
        except (NotLaunched, AlreadyChecking):
            return []
        still = [f for f in summary.failed if not f.unfinished]
        self.resolve(business_id, [n for n in names if n not in {f.check for f in summary.failed}])
        for f in still:
            self.check_alert(business_id, plan.site_host, f)
        return [f.check for f in still]

    def check_alert(self, business_id: int, host: str, f) -> None:
        """One email per problem. A problem that keeps coming back (fail → fine → fail again within a day, or
        fixed by us too many times today) gets ONE "keeps breaking" email, then silence for the rest of the day."""
        since = utcnow() - FLAP_WINDOW
        with Session(self.engine) as s:
            rows = s.exec(select(Alert).where(Alert.business_id == business_id, Alert.key == f.check,
                                              Alert.kind.in_(("check_failed", "check_flapping")))).all()
            if any(a.kind == "check_failed" and a.resolved_at is None for a in rows):
                return  # already told, still open
            recent = [a for a in rows if proof_aware(a.created_at) >= since]
            came_back = any(a.kind == "check_failed" for a in recent)
            told_flapping = any(a.kind == "check_flapping" for a in recent)
            for a in rows:  # yesterday's "keeps breaking" no longer blocks a new one
                if a.kind == "check_flapping" and a.resolved_at is None and proof_aware(a.created_at) < since:
                    a.resolved_at = utcnow()
                    s.add(a)
            s.commit()
        if not (f.keeps_breaking or came_back):
            self.alert(business_id, "check_failed", f.check,
                       subject=f"Something needs attention on {host}",
                       body=(f"Hello,\n\nOur regular check of your website found a problem we couldn't fix by ourselves:\n\n"
                             f"  {f.plain}\n\nSign in to LaunchWitness and open your shop's report to see the details, and "
                             f"press \"Run checks now\" after any change.\n\n— LaunchWitness"))
            return
        note = "(already told today: keeps breaking)"
        if not told_flapping:
            why = ("We fixed it several times today and it broke again, so we've stopped fixing it automatically."
                   if f.keeps_breaking else "It was fine for a while and has now broken again.")
            if not self.alert(business_id, "check_flapping", f.check,
                              subject=f"Something keeps breaking on {host}",
                              body=(f"Hello,\n\nThis keeps breaking on your website:\n\n  {f.plain}\n\n{why} Something "
                                    "outside LaunchWitness is probably changing it back. Sign in to LaunchWitness and open "
                                    "your shop's report for the exact next step. We won't email you about this one again "
                                    "today.\n\n— LaunchWitness")):
                return  # couldn't send: nothing is marked, so the next round tries again
            note = "(in the keeps-breaking email)"
        with Session(self.engine) as s:  # keep the problem itself on record as open, without another email
            s.add(Alert(business_id=business_id, kind="check_failed", key=f.check, sent_to=note))
            s.commit()

    # ---------- alerts ----------

    def resolve(self, business_id: int, names: list[str]) -> None:
        with Session(self.engine) as s:
            for a in s.exec(select(Alert).where(Alert.business_id == business_id, Alert.kind == "check_failed",
                                                Alert.resolved_at == None)).all():  # noqa: E711
                if a.key in names:
                    a.resolved_at = utcnow()
                    s.add(a)
            s.commit()

    def alert(self, business_id: int, kind: str, key: str, *, subject: str, body: str) -> bool:
        """Email the owner's personal address once per (kind, key) until resolved. True if sent."""
        with Session(self.engine) as s:
            b = s.get(Business, business_id)
            open_ = s.exec(select(Alert).where(Alert.business_id == business_id, Alert.kind == kind,
                                               Alert.key == key, Alert.resolved_at == None)).first()  # noqa: E711
            if open_ is not None:
                return False
            to = ", ".join(owner_emails(s, business_id))
            if not to:
                audit.record(s, actor="monitor", action=f"alert_{kind}", target=key, result="skipped",
                             business_id=business_id, detail="the shop has no signed-in owner")
                return False
            try:
                self.integ_for(b).mailer.send(to=to, subject=subject, body=body)
            except Exception as e:
                audit.record(s, actor="monitor", action=f"alert_{kind}", target=key, result="failed",
                             business_id=business_id, detail=type(e).__name__)
                return False
            s.add(Alert(business_id=business_id, kind=kind, key=key, sent_to=to))
            s.commit()
            audit.record(s, actor="monitor", action=f"alert_{kind}", target=key, result="sent",
                         business_id=business_id, detail=subject)
            return True

    def expiry_alerts(self, business_id: int, run_id: int) -> None:
        with Session(self.engine) as s:
            run = s.get(CheckRun, run_id)
            info = json.loads(run.info_json) if run else {}
        self._expiry(business_id, "domain_expiry", info.get("domain_days_left"), DOMAIN_WARN_DAYS,
                     lambda d: (f"Your website name ends in {d} day{'s' if d != 1 else ''}",
                                f"Hello,\n\nYour website name (domain) runs out in {d} day{'s' if d != 1 else ''}. "
                                "Renewing it costs money, so we won't do it for you. Please renew it on godaddy.com "
                                "before then, or your website and order emails will stop working.\n\n— LaunchWitness"))
        self._expiry(business_id, "cert_expiry", info.get("cert_days_left"), CERT_WARN_DAYS,
                     lambda d: (f"Your website's security certificate ends in {d} day{'s' if d != 1 else ''}",
                                f"Hello,\n\nYour website's security certificate (the padlock) runs out in {d} "
                                f"day{'s' if d != 1 else ''} and hasn't renewed itself yet. It costs nothing and you "
                                "don't need to do anything — we're looking into it.\n\n— LaunchWitness"))

    def _expiry(self, business_id: int, kind: str, days: int | None, thresholds: tuple[int, ...], text) -> None:

"""Light monitoring (SPEC §7), with APScheduler.

- Every 15 minutes: site points + opens over HTTPS.
- Daily: the same, plus email settings and "settings unchanged since launch", and
  days left on the certificate and domain.
- A failure is re-checked once a minute later (rule out blips). If it still fails,
  the Doctor explains and applies a safe playbook fix; anything still broken is
  emailed to the owner's PERSONAL email (once per problem until it passes again).
- Domain expiry warnings at 30 / 7 / 1 days (renewal costs money: alert only).
  Certificate warnings at 7 / 1 days (Caddy renews certificates by itself well before that).
- Practice businesses use the fake world, so their "emails" never leave the server.

Switch off with MONITOR_ENABLED=false. Tests never start the scheduler; they call
the job methods directly.
"""

import json
from collections.abc import Callable
from datetime import timedelta

from apscheduler.schedulers.background import BackgroundScheduler
from sqlalchemy.engine import Engine
from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app import audit, renewals
from app.agents.claude_client import Claude
from app.agents.launch_check import AlreadyChecking, NotLaunched, latest_launched_plan, run_checks
from app.config import Settings
from app.integrations import Integrations
from app.models import Alert, Business, CheckRun, utcnow
from app.safety.access import owner_emails

QUICK_MINUTES = 15
RECHECK_SECONDS = 60
SHOP_BUDGET = {"quick": 90, "daily": 300, "recheck": 300}  # seconds one shop may take in a round
FLAP_WINDOW = timedelta(days=1)
QUICK_CHECKS = ["site_points", "https"]
EMAIL_CHECKS = ["email_mx", "email_spf", "email_dkim", "email_dmarc"]  # read-only on shops under the app's domain
DOMAIN_WARN_DAYS = renewals.THRESHOLDS  # one set for everything a person renews (S10)
CERT_WARN_DAYS = renewals.CERT_THRESHOLDS


def daily_checks(mode: str) -> list[str]:
    # The daily test order carries a fresh code. For an inbox we can't read it proves "form accepted ->
    # mail server accepted" only (the report says so); delivery needs the owner's tap on that email.
    return QUICK_CHECKS + EMAIL_CHECKS + ["settings_match", "test_order"]


def proof_aware(when):
    """SQLite hands datetimes back without a timezone; ours are always UTC."""
    return when if when.tzinfo is not None else when.replace(tzinfo=utcnow().tzinfo)


class Monitor:
    def __init__(self, engine: Engine, settings: Settings, integ_for: Callable[[Business], Integrations],
                 claude: Claude, scheduler: BackgroundScheduler | None = None, team: Integrations | None = None):
        self.engine, self.settings, self.integ_for, self.claude = engine, settings, integ_for, claude
        self.team = team  # the server's own integrations: the app domain, the team mailbox, the app zone
        self.scheduler = scheduler or BackgroundScheduler(timezone="UTC")

    # ---------- scheduler wiring ----------

    def register(self) -> None:
        self.scheduler.add_job(self.run_quick, "interval", minutes=QUICK_MINUTES, id="monitor_quick",
                               replace_existing=True, max_instances=1, coalesce=True)
        self.scheduler.add_job(self.run_daily, "interval", days=1, id="monitor_daily",
                               replace_existing=True, max_instances=1, coalesce=True)
        if self.team is not None:
            self.scheduler.add_job(self.watch_addresses, "interval", days=1, id="watch_addresses",
                                   replace_existing=True, max_instances=1, coalesce=True)
            self.scheduler.add_job(self.team_renewals, "interval", days=1, id="team_renewals",
                                   replace_existing=True, max_instances=1, coalesce=True)
            self.scheduler.add_job(self.zone_hygiene, "interval", days=1, id="zone_hygiene",
                                   replace_existing=True, max_instances=1, coalesce=True)

    def start(self) -> None:
        self.register()
        self.scheduler.start()

    def shutdown(self) -> None:
        if self.scheduler.running:
            self.scheduler.shutdown(wait=False)

    def schedule_recheck(self, business_id: int, names: list[str]) -> None:
        self.scheduler.add_job(self.recheck, "date", run_date=utcnow() + timedelta(seconds=RECHECK_SECONDS),
                               args=[business_id, names], id=f"recheck-{business_id}", replace_existing=True)

    # ---------- jobs ----------

    def live_business_ids(self) -> list[int]:
        """Shops to watch: live, not paused. Guest practice shops are short-lived and aren't watched."""
        with Session(self.engine) as s:
            return list(s.exec(select(Business.id).where(Business.status == "live", Business.paused == False,  # noqa: E712
                                                         Business.guest_hash == "")).all())

    def run_quick(self) -> None:
        self._round("quick")

    def run_daily(self) -> None:
        self._round("daily")

    def _round(self, kind: str) -> None:
        """Every live shop, one after the other. A shop whose check blows up is recorded as "couldn't finish"
        (never as passed) and the round carries on with the next shop."""
        for bid in self.live_business_ids():
            try:
                self.check_business(bid, kind)
            except Exception as e:
                with Session(self.engine) as s:
                    audit.record(s, actor="monitor", action="monitor_shop", target=f"business:{bid}", result="failed",
                                 business_id=bid, detail=f"{kind} check couldn't finish: {type(e).__name__}")

    def _context(self, business_id: int):
        with Session(self.engine) as s:
            b = s.get(Business, business_id)
            plan = latest_launched_plan(s, business_id) if b else None
            if b is None or plan is None:
                return None
            s.expunge_all()
            return b, plan

    def check_business(self, business_id: int, kind: str) -> list[str]:
        """Run the quick or daily checks without fixing. Returns the failing check names."""
        found = self._context(business_id)
        if found is None:
            return []
        b, plan = found
        names = QUICK_CHECKS if kind == "quick" else daily_checks(plan.mode)
        try:
            summary = run_checks(self.engine, self.settings, self.integ_for(b), self.claude, plan.id,
                                 trigger=f"monitor_{kind}", names=names, fix=False,
                                 budget_seconds=SHOP_BUDGET[kind])
        except (NotLaunched, AlreadyChecking):  # e.g. the owner just pressed "Run checks now": skip this round
            return []
        # "couldn't finish" / "our lookup failed" is not a failure of the shop: no re-check as one, no alert,
        # and it doesn't clear an open alert either (we simply don't know)
        failing = [f.check for f in summary.failed if not f.unfinished]
        if failing:
            self.schedule_recheck(business_id, failing)
        self.resolve(business_id, [n for n in names if n not in {f.check for f in summary.failed}])
        if kind == "daily":
            self.expiry_alerts(business_id, summary.run_id)
        return failing

    def recheck(self, business_id: int, names: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        """A minute later: re-check; the Doctor fixes what it safely can; alert on what's left."""
        found = self._context(business_id)
        if found is None:
            return []
        b, plan = found
        try:
            summary = run_checks(self.engine, self.settings, self.integ_for(b), self.claude, plan.id,
                                 trigger="monitor_recheck", names=names, fix=True,
                                 budget_seconds=SHOP_BUDGET["recheck"])
        except (NotLaunched, AlreadyChecking):
            return []
        still = [f for f in summary.failed if not f.unfinished]
        self.resolve(business_id, [n for n in names if n not in {f.check for f in summary.failed}])
        for f in still:
            self.check_alert(business_id, plan.site_host, f)
        return [f.check for f in still]

    def check_alert(self, business_id: int, host: str, f) -> None:
        """One email per problem. A problem that keeps coming back (fail → fine → fail again within a day, or
        fixed by us too many times today) gets ONE "keeps breaking" email, then silence for the rest of the day."""
        since = utcnow() - FLAP_WINDOW
        with Session(self.engine) as s:
            rows = s.exec(select(Alert).where(Alert.business_id == business_id, Alert.key == f.check,
                                              Alert.kind.in_(("check_failed", "check_flapping")))).all()
            if any(a.kind == "check_failed" and a.resolved_at is None for a in rows):
                return  # already told, still open
            recent = [a for a in rows if proof_aware(a.created_at) >= since]
            came_back = any(a.kind == "check_failed" for a in recent)
            told_flapping = any(a.kind == "check_flapping" for a in recent)
            for a in rows:  # yesterday's "keeps breaking" no longer blocks a new one

                    a.resolved_at = utcnow()

            s.commit()
        if not (f.keeps_breaking or came_back):

                       subject=f"Something needs attention on {host}",
                       body=(f"Hello,\n\nOur regular check of your website found a problem we couldn't fix by ourselves:\n\n"
                             f"  {f.plain}\n\nSign in to LaunchWitness and open your shop's report to see the details, and "
                             f"press \"Run checks now\" after any change.\n\n— LaunchWitness"))

        note = "(already told today: keeps breaking)"
        if not told_flapping:

    def resolve(self, business_id: int, names: list[str]) -> None:

                    s.add(a)

        """Email the owner's personal address once per (kind, key) until resolved. True if sent."""
        with Session(self.engine) as s:
            b = s.get(Business, business_id)
            open_ = s.exec(select(Alert).where(Alert.business_id == business_id, Alert.kind == kind,
                                               Alert.key == key, Alert.resolved_at == None)).first()  # noqa: E711
            if open_ is not None:

            to = ", ".join(owner_emails(s, business_id))

                             business_id=business_id, detail="the shop has no signed-in owner")
                return False
            try:

            except Exception as e:

                             business_id=business_id, detail=type(e).__name__)

                                f"Hello,\n\nYour website name (domain) runs out in {d} day{'s' if d != 1 else ''}. "
                                "Renewing it costs money, so we won't do it for you. Please renew it on godaddy.com "
                                "before then, or your website and order emails will stop working.\n\n— LaunchWitness"))
        self._expiry(business_id, "cert_expiry", info.get("cert_days_left"), CERT_WARN_DAYS,

"""Send mail through the app's one mailbox (GoDaddy Professional Email, secureserver.net).

Port 465 = implicit SSL (default). Port 587 = STARTTLS. If an SSL connection to 465 can't be
made at all (blocked port, timeout, TLS handshake error), we try 587 STARTTLS once. We never
fall back after login has started, so a message can't be sent twice and a wrong password
isn't retried. Host, port, user and password come only from settings (env vars).
"""

import logging
import smtplib
import ssl
from email.message import EmailMessage
from email.utils import make_msgid
from typing import Protocol

from app.config import Settings

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

STARTTLS_PORT = 587
TIMEOUT_S = 30


class Mailer(Protocol):
    def send(self, *, to: str, subject: str, body: str, html: str | None = None) -> str: ...


class SmtpMailer:
    def __init__(self, settings: Settings):
        self.host = settings.smtp_host
        self.port = settings.smtp_port
        self.user = settings.smtp_user
        self._password = settings.smtp_password
        self.security = settings.smtp_security

    def _connect(self) -> smtplib.SMTP:
        if self.security == "plain":  # local catch-all only (config refuses it for real host names)
            return smtplib.SMTP(self.host, self.port, timeout=TIMEOUT_S)
        context = ssl.create_default_context()
        if self.port != STARTTLS_PORT and self.security == "ssl":
            try:
                return smtplib.SMTP_SSL(self.host, self.port, context=context, timeout=TIMEOUT_S)
            except (ConnectionError, TimeoutError, ssl.SSLError, smtplib.SMTPConnectError,
                    smtplib.SMTPServerDisconnected) as e:
                log.warning("SMTP SSL to %s:%s failed (%s); trying port %s with STARTTLS",
                            self.host, self.port, type(e).__name__, STARTTLS_PORT)

def check_order_limits(session: Session, settings: Settings, business: Business, visitor: str) -> None:
    """Per visitor (hashed IP) per shop per hour, and per shop per day. Test orders don't count."""
    real = (Order.business_id == business.id, Order.is_test == False)  # noqa: E712
    now = utcnow()
    mine = session.exec(select(func.count()).select_from(Order).where(
        *real, Order.visitor == visitor, Order.created_at >= now - timedelta(hours=1))).one()
    shop = session.exec(select(func.count()).select_from(Order).where(
        *real, Order.created_at >= now - timedelta(days=1))).one()
    if mine >= settings.orders_per_visitor_per_hour or shop >= settings.orders_per_shop_per_day:
        audit.record(session, actor="customer", action="order_placed", target=f"business:{business.id}",
                     result="blocked", business_id=business.id,
                     detail="visitor hourly limit" if mine >= settings.orders_per_visitor_per_hour else "shop daily limit")
        raise TooManyOrders


TOKEN = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}$")


def existing_order(session: Session, business: Business, token: str) -> Order | None:
    """The order already made with this form token (a double tap or a re-sent form), if any."""
    if not TOKEN.match(token):
        return None
    return session.exec(select(Order).where(Order.business_id == business.id, Order.client_token == token)).first()


def order_view(order: Order) -> dict:
    return {"customer_name": order.customer_name, "customer_phone": order.customer_phone, "note": order.note,
            "items": json.loads(order.items_json), "total_inr": order.total_inr, "ref": order.ref}


def place_order(session: Session, mailer: Mailer, settings: Settings, *, business: Business, profile: Profile,
                data: dict, is_test: bool = False, nonce: str = "", visitor: str = "", token: str = "",
                confirm_url: str = "") -> Order:
    """Store the order, then email it to `order_recipients`. The launch check's test order and a
    customer's order both come through here, so a passing test order proves the real path."""
    order = Order(business_id=business.id, customer_name=data["customer_name"], customer_phone=data["customer_phone"],
                  items_json=json.dumps(data["items"], ensure_ascii=False), total_inr=data["total_inr"],
                  note=data["note"], is_test=is_test, nonce=nonce, visitor=visitor, ref=new_ref(),
                  client_token=token if TOKEN.match(token) else "")
    session.add(order)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(order)
    audit.record(session, actor="checker" if is_test else "customer", action="order_placed", target=f"order:{order.id}", result="ok",
                 business_id=business.id, detail=f"{len(data['items'])} item(s), total {data['total_inr']}")

    recipients = order_recipients(session, settings, business)
    orders_url = f"{settings.app_base_url.rstrip('/')}/#/b/{business.id}/orders"
    subject, body = order_email(business, profile, order, data["items"], confirm_url, orders_url)
    try:
        order.email_message_id = mailer.send(to=", ".join(recipients), subject=subject, body=body)
        order.email_status = "sent"
        result, detail = "ok", f"to {len(recipients)} address(es), {order.email_message_id}"
    except Exception as e:  # keep the order even if the mail server is down
        order.email_status = "failed"
        result, detail = "failed", type(e).__name__
    session.add(order)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(order)
    audit.record(session, actor="system", action="order_email", target=f"order:{order.id}", result=result,

    checker's practice test order both come through here, so the test order exercises the real path.

    A POST carrying `lw_test=<nonce>` of an OPEN test ticket for this shop becomes a hidden test order

import logging

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request, Response

NO_EMAIL = "We couldn't send the email right now. Please try again in a few minutes."


class LinkRequest(BaseModel):
    email: str = Field(max_length=254)
    next: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=200)


def send_link(settings: Settings, mailer: Mailer, session: Session, *, kind: str, email: str, page: str, raw: str,
              next_: str = "") -> dict:
    """Email the link. In DEV_MODE (local only) nothing is emailed and the link is returned instead.
    If the mail server is down we say so: we never pretend an email went out."""
    url = accounts.link_url(settings, page, raw, next_)
    if settings.dev_mode:
        return {"dev_link": url}
    subject, text, html = accounts.link_email(kind, url)
    try:
        mailer.send(to=email, subject=subject, body=text, html=html)
    except Exception as e:
        log.warning("could not send %s email: %s", kind, type(e).__name__)
        audit.record(session, actor="system", action=f"{kind}_email", result="failed", detail=type(e).__name__)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail=NO_EMAIL) from e
    audit.record(session, actor="system", action=f"{kind}_email", result="sent")
    return {}


@router.post("/auth/request-link")
def request_link(body: LinkRequest, request: Request, settings: Annotated[Settings, Depends(get_settings)],
                 session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)],
                 mailer: Annotated[Mailer, Depends(get_mailer)]) -> dict:
    """Always the same answer, whether or not the address has an account, so nobody can find out which emails do."""
    email = accounts.normalize_email(body.email)
    if email is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="That email address doesn't look right. Please check it.")
    visitor = visitor_id(request)
    if accounts.links_last_hour(session, visitor) >= settings.signin_links_per_ip_per_hour:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=429, detail="Too many sign-in links were asked for from here. "
                            "Please wait an hour and try again.")
    out = {"ok": True, "message": accounts.SAME_ANSWER}
    user = accounts.find_user(session, email)
    if user is not None and user.status not in ACTIVE:  # suspended: no link, same answer
        return out
    if accounts.links_today(session, email) >= settings.signin_links_per_email_per_day:
        audit.record(session, actor="system", action="login_email", result="blocked", detail="daily limit for one address")
        return out  # same answer; the limit protects the inbox from being flooded
    raw = accounts.issue_token(session, email, "login", visitor)
    out.update(send_link(settings, mailer, session, kind="login", email=email, page="signin/confirm", raw=raw,
                         next_=accounts.safe_next(body.next)))
    return out

"""Startup reconciler: launches and check runs are worked on by this process. If the server
restarts in the middle, nothing would ever finish them, and the screens would say "running"
forever. On start we close them honestly: the plan becomes failed with "press Resume", and a
stuck check run becomes done / not passed.
"""

import json

from sqlalchemy.engine import Engine
from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app import audit
from app.models import CheckRun, Plan, utcnow

RESTART_MESSAGE = "The server restarted during your launch. Nothing was lost: press Resume to continue."


def reconcile(engine: Engine) -> dict:
    """Returns how many rows were closed: {"plans": n, "check_runs": n}."""
    with Session(engine) as s:
        plans = s.exec(select(Plan).where(Plan.status.in_(("approved", "running")))).all()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        for plan in plans:
            steps = json.loads(plan.steps_json)
            hit = next((st for st in steps if st["status"] == "running"), None) or \
                next((st for st in steps if st["status"] == "pending"), None)
            if hit is not None:
                hit.update(status="failed", message=RESTART_MESSAGE, finished_at=utcnow().isoformat())
            plan.steps_json, plan.status = json.dumps(steps), "failed"
            s.add(plan)
            audit.record(s, actor="system", action="reconcile", target=f"plan:{plan.id}", result="failed",
                         business_id=plan.business_id, detail="server restarted while this launch was running")
        runs = s.exec(select(CheckRun).where(CheckRun.status == "running")).all()
        for run in runs:
            run.status, run.passed, run.finished_at = "done", False, utcnow()
            s.add(run)
            audit.record(s, actor="system", action="reconcile", target=f"run:{run.id}", result="failed",
                         business_id=run.business_id, detail="server restarted while these checks were running")
        s.commit()
        return {"plans": len(plans), "check_runs": len(runs)}

content.content:
"""Checker (code only): proves a finished launch works (SPEC §6).

Checks: site points to the server (asked of the AUTHORITATIVE nameservers via
`integ.dns`), site opens over HTTPS with a valid certificate, email settings
(MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC of the domain the order mailbox is on, compared with the
mail provider table; read-only), and a real test order arrives. Each result is
stored as a CheckResult row and an AuditEvent. Launch steps are not a check:
the report shows them separately.
"""

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import timedelta
from urllib.parse import urljoin

from sqlmodel import Session

from app import audit, proof
from app.agents.executor import Ctx
from app.agents.planner import DKIM_PENDING
from app.agents.reader import Profile
from app.checks.dns_resolver import lookup
from app.mail.providers import provider_for
from app.models import CheckResult, Order, utcnow
from app.sites.orders import order_recipients


@dataclass
class Outcome:
    check: str
    passed: bool
    plain: str  # one line for the seller
    detail: str = ""  # technical
    waiting: bool = False  # passed as far as we can see, but delivery still needs the owner's "Yes, I got it"
    unfinished: bool = False  # we couldn't complete it (our lookup failed, or time ran out): not passed, not her fault
    keeps_breaking: bool = False  # fixed several times today and broken again: automatic fixing has stopped


class CouldntCheck(Exception):
    """Something on OUR side failed, so the check has no answer. Never a failure of the shop."""


OUR_SIDE = ("We couldn't look this up just now. The problem is on our side, not yours, and nothing about your shop has "
            "changed. We'll check again on the next round.")
OUT_OF_TIME = "This check couldn't finish in time, so we don't know yet. We'll try again on the next round."


def dns_values(ctx: Ctx, name: str, rtype: str) -> list[str]:
    """One DNS answer for a check. A lookup that failed on our side raises, so it can't be read as "missing"."""
    got = lookup(ctx.integ.dns, name, rtype)
    if got.status == "error":
        raise CouldntCheck(f"{rtype} {name}: our lookup failed")
    return list(got.values)


def practice_world(ctx: Ctx) -> bool:
    return bool(ctx.integ.fake or ctx.business.practice)


def evidence(ctx: Ctx, check: str, step: str, **fields) -> None:
    ok = any(v.startswith("v=spf1") and provider.spf_include in v for v in got)
    return Outcome("email_spf", ok, "Your mailbox is allowed to send email for you." if ok else
                   "Your emails may land in spam: the sending permission is missing.",
                   f"TXT {zone} = {got or 'nothing'}; expected {provider.spf_include}")


def dkim_names(ctx: Ctx, zone: str) -> list[str]:
    """Signing record names: the ones this launch planned, else whatever the live zone has."""
    names = [c["name"] for c in ctx.changes if c["name"].endswith("._domainkey")]
    if not names:
        try:
            names = sorted({r["name"] for r in ctx.integ.godaddy.get_records(zone) if r["name"].endswith("._domainkey")})
        except Exception:  # can't list the zone (not ours): fall back to the provider's usual names
            names = []
    return names or [f"{sel}._domainkey" for sel in provider_for(ctx.settings).dkim_selectors]


def check_email_dkim(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    zone = mail_zone(ctx)
    names, seen = dkim_names(ctx, zone), {}
    for name in names:
        txt = _txt(dns_values(ctx, f"{name}.{zone}", "TXT"))
        seen[name] = (any(v.startswith("v=DKIM1") and "p=" in v for v in txt)
                      or bool(dns_values(ctx, f"{name}.{zone}", "CNAME")))
    ok = bool(seen) and all(seen.values())
    return Outcome("email_dkim", ok, "Your emails are signed so customers can trust them." if ok else
                   "Your emails aren't signed, so they may land in spam.",
                   f"signing records on {zone}: {seen or 'none found'}")


def check_email_dmarc(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    zone = mail_zone(ctx)
    got = _txt(dns_values(ctx, f"_dmarc.{zone}", "TXT"))
    ok = any(v.startswith("v=DMARC1") for v in got)
    return Outcome("email_dmarc", ok, "Fake emails in your name will be treated as spam." if ok else
                   "Order emails could land in spam: a protection setting is missing.",
                   f"TXT _dmarc.{zone} = {got or 'nothing'}")


TEST_CUSTOMER = {"customer_name": "LaunchWitness test", "customer_phone": "0000000000",
                 "note": "Automatic test order from your launch check. No action needed."}


def check_test_order(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    """Order from the shop like a customer: open the public page, find the order form, post it with a
    one-time test code, then record each hop separately. Delivery is proven only by finding the email in
    an inbox we can read, or by the owner tapping "Yes, I got it"; a mail server's "accepted" is not delivery."""
    url = f"https://{ctx.plan.site_host}/"
    web = shop_web(ctx)
    profile = Profile.model_validate_json(ctx.business.profile_json)
    page = web.get(url)
    form = proof.find_order_form(page.html) if page.status == 200 else None
    if form is None:
        return Outcome("test_order", False, "We couldn't open your order form for a test order.",
                       f"GET {url}: status {page.status} {page.error}".strip())
    index = next((i for i, x in enumerate(profile.products) if not x.addon), 0)
    field = f"qty_{index}"
    if field not in form.qty_fields:
        return Outcome("test_order", False, "We couldn't find an item to order on your page.", f"{field} not in form")

class CouldntCheck(Exception):
    """Something on OUR side failed, so the check has no answer. Never a failure of the shop."""

        except Exception:  # can't list the zone (not ours): fall back to the provider's usual names

# Production-like stack on your own computer: HTTPS through Caddy (its own local CA), real cookies
# (DEV_MODE=false), the pretend GoDaddy world (USE_FAKES=true), saved Claude answers, and every email
# caught by Mailpit (nothing leaves the machine). It never reads ../.env.
#
#   docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.local.yml up -d --build
#
# App:    https://launchwitness.localhost       (shops: https://<slug>.launchwitness.localhost)
# Mail:   http://localhost:8025                  (Mailpit inbox; sign-in links arrive here)
# Details and checks: deploy/README.md

name: launchwitness-local

services:
  app:
    env_file: !reset []
    environment:
      APP_DOMAIN: launchwitness.localhost
      APP_BASE_URL: https://launchwitness.localhost
      ADMIN_EMAIL: admin@launchwitness.localhost
      ADMIN_TOKEN: ${LOCAL_ADMIN_TOKEN:-local-stack-only-admin-token}
      DEV_MODE: "false"
      USE_FAKES: "true"
      CLAUDE_MODE: fixture
      SERVER_IP: 127.0.0.1
      MONITOR_ENABLED: "true"
      PRACTICE_STEP_SECONDS: ${PRACTICE_STEP_SECONDS:-0}
      SMTP_HOST: mailpit
      SMTP_PORT: "1025"
      SMTP_SECURITY: plain
      SMTP_USER: hello@launchwitness.localhost
      IMAP_USER: hello@launchwitness.localhost
      # The e2e suite signs up several people from one address; keep the real limits otherwise.
      SIGNIN_LINKS_PER_IP_PER_HOUR: "200"
      SIGNIN_LINKS_PER_EMAIL_PER_DAY: "100"
      VISITOR_CONTACTS_PER_DAY: "100"
      USER_DESCRIBES_PER_DAY: "50"
      VISITOR_DESCRIBES_PER_DAY: "50"
      VISITOR_LAUNCHES_PER_DAY: "50"
    depends_on:
      - mailpit

  caddy:
    environment:
      APP_DOMAIN: launchwitness.localhost
      CADDY_EXTRA_GLOBAL: local_certs

  mailpit:
    image: axllent/mailpit:v1.21.8
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8025:8025"   # web inbox + API, this computer only
    environment:
      MP_SMTP_AUTH_ACCEPT_ANY: "1"
      MP_SMTP_AUTH_ALLOW_INSECURE: "1"
    restart: unless-stopped

from datetime import timedelta
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app.config import Settings, get_settings
from app.db import get_session
from app.models import AuditEvent, utcnow
from app.safety.access import ActorDep
from app.selfcheck import mailbox_warning, warnings  # noqa: F401  (mailbox_warning: re-exported for callers)

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api", tags=["health"])


def unsent_alerts(session: Session) -> int:
    """Alert emails that couldn't be sent in the last day and haven't gone out since (our mail service was down)."""
    since = utcnow() - timedelta(days=1)
    rows = session.exec(select(AuditEvent).where(AuditEvent.actor == "monitor", AuditEvent.created_at >= since,
                                                 AuditEvent.result.in_(("failed", "sent")),
                                                 AuditEvent.action.like("%alert%")).order_by(AuditEvent.id)).all()
    last = {(e.action, e.target, e.business_id, e.user_id): e.result for e in rows}
    return sum(1 for result in last.values() if result == "failed")


@router.get("/health")
def health(settings: Annotated[Settings, Depends(get_settings)], actor: ActorDep,
           session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]) -> dict:
    """Liveness + the startup self-check. Anyone sees the harmless warnings; the admin sees all of them.
    Never a secret value."""
    out: dict = {"ok": True, "env": settings.godaddy_env}
    found = [w for w in warnings(settings) if w.public or actor.is_admin]
    texts, codes = [w.text for w in found], [w.code for w in found]
    unsent = unsent_alerts(session) if actor.is_admin else 0
    if unsent:
        texts.append(f"{unsent} alert email{'s' if unsent != 1 else ''} couldn't be sent in the last day (our mail "
                     "service refused or was unreachable). Each is tried again on the next monitoring round.")
        codes.append("alerts_unsent")
    if texts:
        out["warnings"], out["warning_codes"] = texts, codes
    return out
def test_fail_alert_recover_fail_again_sends_one_keeps_breaking_email_then_goes_quiet(client, integ, engine, monitor):
    biz = meera(client)
    approve(client, plan(client, biz))
    set_email(engine, biz["id"])

    def cycle():
        integ.http.broken_cert.add("meera.localhost")
        monitor.check_business(biz["id"], "quick")
        monitor.recheck(biz["id"], ["https"])
        integ.http.broken_cert.clear()
        monitor.check_business(biz["id"], "quick")  # recovers: the alert is resolved

    cycle()
    assert len(told(integ)) == 1 and "keeps breaking" not in told(integ)[-1]["subject"]
    cycle()
    assert len(told(integ)) == 2 and "keeps breaking" in told(integ)[-1]["subject"]
    for _ in range(4):
        cycle()
    assert len(told(integ)) == 2  # no email storm, however often it flaps today
    kinds = [k for k, _key, _to in alerts(engine)]
    assert kinds.count("check_flapping") == 1


# ---------- 5. failures of our own ----------

def test_alert_that_could_not_be_sent_is_recorded_retried_and_shown_to_the_team(client, integ, engine, monitor):
    biz = meera(client)
    approve(client, plan(client, biz))
    set_email(engine, biz["id"])
    integ.http.broken_cert.add("meera.localhost")
    integ.mailer.fail = True  # our own mail service is down
    assert monitor.recheck(biz["id"], ["https"]) == ["https"]
    assert alerts(engine) == []  # not marked as sent
    with Session(engine) as s:
        assert s.exec(select(AuditEvent).where(AuditEvent.action == "alert_check_failed",
                                               AuditEvent.result == "failed")).first() is not None
    admin = {"X-Admin-Token": ADMIN_TOKEN}
    assert "alerts_unsent" in client.get("/api/health", headers=admin).json().get("warning_codes", [])
    assert "alerts_unsent" not in client.get("/api/health").json().get("warning_codes", [])  # the team only
    integ.mailer.fail = False
    assert monitor.recheck(biz["id"], ["https"]) == ["https"]  # the next run tries again
    assert [k for k, _key, _to in alerts(engine)] == ["check_failed"] and len(told(integ)) == 1
    assert "alerts_unsent" not in client.get("/api/health", headers=admin).json().get("warning_codes", [])


def test_watch_alert_that_could_not_be_sent_is_retried(engine, mailer):

"""SQLite tables. Fields are minimal for M0 and will grow per milestone."""

from datetime import UTC, datetime

from sqlmodel import Field, SQLModel


def utcnow() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(UTC)


class User(SQLModel, table=True):
class Alert(SQLModel, table=True):
    """An email sent to the owner by monitoring. Used so each warning is sent once."""

    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
    business_id: int = Field(foreign_key="business.id", index=True)
    kind: str  # check_failed | domain_expiry | cert_expiry
    key: str  # e.g. the check name, or "<expiry date>:<days threshold>"
    sent_to: str = ""
    resolved_at: datetime | None = None  # check_failed: set when the check passes again
    created_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=utcnow)


class Order(SQLModel, table=True):
    """An order a customer placed through a seller's site form (no payment taken)."""

    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
    business_id: int = Field(foreign_key="business.id", index=True)
    customer_name: str
    customer_phone: str
    items_json: str = "[]"  # [{"name", "qty", "price_inr"}]
    total_inr: int = 0
    note: str = ""
    ref: str = Field(default="", index=True)  # public order reference, e.g. LW-4F2K7Q9M (random, not a count)
    is_test: bool = False  # placed by the launch check, not a customer
    nonce: str = ""  # test orders: random code in the email subject + body, so an old email can never pass
    visitor: str = Field(default="", index=True)  # hashed client IP (order rate limit); never the IP itself
    client_token: str = Field(default="", index=True)  # hidden form field: a double submit makes one order
    email_status: str = "pending"  # pending | sent | failed
    email_message_id: str = ""
    # S10.5: the owner's own progress on the order (sites/orders.py STATUS_STEPS). Only the owner sets it.
    status: str = Field(default="new", index=True)  # new | confirmed | paid | done | cancelled
    status_changed_at: datetime | None = None
    created_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=utcnow)

"""S13: the durable email outbox. Every email the app sends is saved here first, then sent.

- `send(...)`: save the email under a unique key (the same order / alert / link is never saved or sent twice),
  then try it at once with a short timeout while the person waits. If that fails, the sender job keeps trying.
- `run_once(...)`: the sender job (one process, in the monitor's scheduler): claims each due email atomically,
  sends it, and on a temporary error waits longer each time (exponential backoff with jitter). A permanent
  error (the server refused that recipient, a bad address) or too many tries makes it `dead`, shown to the team.
- Priorities: 0 = sign-in links + orders (never held back), 1 = alerts + team mail, 2 = test orders + the digest.
  `SMTP_DAILY_LIMIT` is the budget for the real mail server: from 80% priority 2 waits, at 100% priority 1 waits.
  Practice mail (the pretend world) never leaves the server and doesn't count.
- A sign-in link that would arrive expired is dropped, and its body (which holds the link) is emptied.
- `reconcile(...)`: at startup, mail left `sending` by a crash goes back to the queue. It may have been sent just
  before the crash, so it can arrive twice; it keeps the same Message-ID, so mail apps show it once.

Nothing here logs or stores a secret or a body in `last_error`: only the error kind and the SMTP code.
"""

import json
import random
import smtplib
from collections.abc import Callable
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from email.utils import make_msgid

from sqlalchemy import func, update
from sqlalchemy.engine import Engine
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app import audit
from app.config import Settings
from app.mail.smtp import Mailer
from app.models import Order, Outbox, utcnow

PRIORITY = {"login": 0, "order": 0, "alert": 1, "team": 1, "watch": 1, "contact": 1, "test_order": 2, "digest": 2}
LOW_SHARE = 0.8  # from this share of the daily budget, priority-2 mail waits
BASE_DELAY_S, MAX_DELAY_S, MAX_ATTEMPTS = 30, 30 * 60, 10  # about 2 hours of trying, then dead
HOLD_S = 15 * 60  # mail held back by the budget looks again after this
STALE_SENDING = timedelta(minutes=10)  # a claim older than this lost its sender (it can't still be talking)
NOW_TIMEOUT_S = {"login": 5.0, "order": 10.0}  # trying at once while a person waits; others 15 s
JOB_TIMEOUT_S = 30.0
LINK_MARGIN = timedelta(minutes=2)  # a sign-in link must arrive with at least this long left to use it
OPEN = ("queued", "failed")


def aware(when: datetime | None) -> datetime | None:
    return when if when is None or when.tzinfo is not None else when.replace(tzinfo=UTC)


def start_of_day(now: datetime | None = None) -> datetime:
    now = now or utcnow()
    return now.replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)


def channel_of(integ) -> str:
    """Practice integrations (the pretend world) never reach the real mail server."""
    return "practice" if getattr(integ, "fake", False) else "smtp"


# ---------- saving ----------

def enqueue(session: Session, settings: Settings, *, kind: str, key: str, to: str, subject: str, body: str,
            html: str = "", channel: str = "smtp", business_id: int | None = None, order_id: int | None = None,
            user_id: int | None = None, ref: dict | None = None, expires_at: datetime | None = None) -> tuple[Outbox, bool]:
    """Save an email once. Returns (row, created). An existing key returns the existing row unchanged."""
    found = session.exec(select(Outbox).where(Outbox.key == key)).first()
    if found is not None:
        return found, False
    ref = dict(ref or {})
    ref.setdefault("planned_id", make_msgid(domain=settings.smtp_user.rsplit("@", 1)[-1] or "launchwitness.com"))
    row = Outbox(key=key, kind=kind, priority=PRIORITY.get(kind, 1), channel=channel, to_addr=to, subject=subject,
                 body=body, html=html or "", business_id=business_id, order_id=order_id, user_id=user_id,
                 ref_json=json.dumps(ref), expires_at=expires_at)
    session.add(row)
    try:
        session.commit()
    except IntegrityError:  # the same key saved a moment ago by someone else: theirs wins
        session.rollback()
        return session.exec(select(Outbox).where(Outbox.key == key)).one(), False
    session.refresh(row)
    _settle(session, row)
    return row, True


def send(session: Session, settings: Settings, mailer: Mailer, *, retry_now: bool = False,
         timeout: float | None = None, **fields) -> Outbox:
    """Save (once) and try at once. `retry_now`: a row already saved and not yet sent is tried again now
    (the caller's own round is the retry, e.g. monitoring). Returns the row as it is afterwards."""
    row, created = enqueue(session, settings, **fields)
    if row.status in OPEN and (created or retry_now):
        row = attempt(session, settings, mailer, row.id, timeout=timeout or NOW_TIMEOUT_S.get(row.kind, 15.0),
                      ignore_backoff=True)
    return row


# ---------- sending ----------

def sent_today(session: Session, now: datetime | None = None) -> int:
    return session.exec(select(func.count()).select_from(Outbox).where(
        Outbox.channel == "smtp", Outbox.status == "sent", Outbox.sent_at >= start_of_day(now))).one()


def held_by_budget(session: Session, settings: Settings, row: Outbox, now: datetime | None = None) -> bool:
    if row.channel != "smtp" or row.priority == 0:
        return False  # sign-in links and orders are never held back; practice mail isn't real mail
    used, limit = sent_today(session, now), max(settings.smtp_daily_limit, 0)
    return used >= (limit if row.priority == 1 else limit * LOW_SHARE)


def permanent(e: Exception) -> bool:
    """Errors that another try can't fix. A refused sign-in is NOT permanent: the team can fix the password."""
    if isinstance(e, smtplib.SMTPRecipientsRefused):
        return bool(e.recipients) and all(int(code) >= 500 for code, _ in e.recipients.values())
    if isinstance(e, smtplib.SMTPAuthenticationError):
        return False
    if isinstance(e, smtplib.SMTPResponseException):
        return 500 <= int(e.smtp_code) < 600
    return isinstance(e, (ValueError, UnicodeError))


def error_text(e: Exception) -> str:
    """Kind + SMTP code only: the server's words can contain addresses."""
    code = getattr(e, "smtp_code", None)
    if isinstance(e, smtplib.SMTPRecipientsRefused) and e.recipients:
        code = ",".join(sorted({str(c) for c, _ in e.recipients.values()}))
    return f"{type(e).__name__}{f' {code}' if code else ''}"[:120]


def backoff(attempts: int) -> float:
    return min(MAX_DELAY_S, BASE_DELAY_S * 2 ** max(attempts - 1, 0)) * random.uniform(0.8, 1.2)


def claim(session: Session, row_id: int, now: datetime, ignore_backoff: bool = False) -> bool:
    """Atomic: only one sender can move a row to `sending` (one UPDATE with the status in its WHERE)."""
    cond = [Outbox.id == row_id, Outbox.status.in_(OPEN)]
    if not ignore_backoff:
        cond.append(Outbox.next_try_at <= now)
    result = session.exec(update(Outbox).where(*cond).values(  # type: ignore[call-overload]
        status="sending", claimed_at=now, attempts=Outbox.attempts + 1, updated_at=now))
    session.commit()
    return result.rowcount == 1


def attempt(session: Session, settings: Settings, mailer: Mailer, row_id: int, *, timeout: float = JOB_TIMEOUT_S,
            ignore_backoff: bool = False, now: datetime | None = None) -> Outbox:
    now = now or utcnow()
    row = session.get(Outbox, row_id)
    if row is None or row.status not in OPEN:
        return row
    if row.expires_at is not None and aware(row.expires_at) <= now:
        return _finish(session, row, "dead", now, error="expired before it could be sent: dropped")
    if held_by_budget(session, settings, row, now):
        row.next_try_at, row.last_error, row.updated_at = now + timedelta(seconds=HOLD_S), "waiting: daily send budget", now
        session.add(row)
        session.commit()
        return row
    if not claim(session, row_id, now, ignore_backoff):
        session.refresh(row)
        return row  # someone else has it (or it isn't due): never two sends
    session.refresh(row)
    ref = json.loads(row.ref_json or "{}")
    try:
        message_id = mailer.send(to=row.to_addr, subject=row.subject, body=row.body, html=row.html or None,
                                 message_id=ref.get("planned_id"), timeout=timeout)
    except Exception as e:
        if permanent(e) or row.attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS:
            return _finish(session, row, "dead", utcnow(), error=error_text(e))
        row.next_try_at = utcnow() + timedelta(seconds=backoff(row.attempts))
        return _finish(session, row, "failed", utcnow(), error=error_text(e))
    row.message_id, row.sent_at = str(message_id or ""), utcnow()
    return _finish(session, row, "sent", row.sent_at)


def _finish(session: Session, row: Outbox, status: str, now: datetime, error: str = "") -> Outbox:
    row.status, row.updated_at, row.claimed_at = status, now, None
    if error:
        row.last_error = error
    elif status == "sent":
        row.last_error = ""
    if status in ("sent", "dead") and row.kind == "login":
        row.body = row.html = ""  # the link is a key to the account: don't keep it once it's out (or dropped)
    session.add(row)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(row)
    _settle(session, row)
    return row


def order_email_status(status: str) -> str:
    return {"sent": "sent", "dead": "failed", "failed": "retrying"}.get(status, "queued")


def _settle(session: Session, row: Outbox) -> None:
    """What the rest of the app sees: the order's email status, the watched problems, the audit trail."""
    ref = json.loads(row.ref_json or "{}")
    if row.order_id is not None:
        order = session.get(Order, row.order_id)
        if order is not None:
            order.email_status = order_email_status(row.status)
            order.email_message_id = row.message_id if row.status == "sent" else ""
            session.add(order)
            session.commit()
    if row.kind == "watch" and row.status == "sent" and ref.get("watch_id"):
        from app.models import WatchedAddress

        w = session.get(WatchedAddress, ref["watch_id"])
        if w is not None:  # told now: these problems are known (the daily run forgot them when the first try failed)
            w.problems_json = json.dumps(sorted(set(json.loads(w.problems_json or "[]")) | set(ref.get("problems", []))))
            session.add(w)
            session.commit()
    a = ref.get("audit")
    if a and row.status in ("sent", "failed", "dead"):
        audit.record(session, actor=a.get("actor", "system"), action=a["action"], target=a.get("target", ""),
                     result=row.status if row.status != "dead" else "failed", business_id=row.business_id,
                     user_id=row.user_id, detail=f"outbox:{row.id} {row.last_error or row.message_id}"[:200])


# ---------- the sender job ----------

def run_once(engine: Engine, settings: Settings, mailer_for: Callable[[str], Mailer], now: datetime | None = None,
             batch: int = 40) -> dict[str, int]:
    """One pass: free stale claims, then send every due email, most important first. Returns counts by result."""
    now = now or utcnow()
    out: dict[str, int] = {}
    with Session(engine) as s:
        stale = s.exec(update(Outbox).where(Outbox.status == "sending",  # type: ignore[call-overload]
                                            Outbox.claimed_at < now - STALE_SENDING).values(
            status="failed", claimed_at=None, last_error="sender stopped mid-send: trying again", updated_at=now))
        s.commit()
        if stale.rowcount:
            out["reclaimed"] = stale.rowcount
        ids = s.exec(select(Outbox.id).where(Outbox.status.in_(OPEN), Outbox.next_try_at <= now)
                     .order_by(Outbox.priority, Outbox.created_at).limit(batch)).all()
    for row_id in ids:
        with Session(engine) as s:
            row = s.get(Outbox, row_id)
            if row is None:
                continue
            try:
                done = attempt(s, settings, mailer_for(row.channel), row_id, now=now)
            except Exception:  # one bad row never stops the others
                out["error"] = out.get("error", 0) + 1
                continue
            label = done.status if done.last_error != "waiting: daily send budget" else "held"
            out[label] = out.get(label, 0) + 1
    return out


def reconcile(session: Session) -> int:
    """Startup: mail left `sending` by a crash is queued again (same Message-ID)."""
    now = utcnow()
    result = session.exec(update(Outbox).where(Outbox.status == "sending").values(  # type: ignore[call-overload]
        status="failed", claimed_at=None, next_try_at=now, updated_at=now,
        last_error="server restarted while sending: trying again (it may already have arrived)"))
    session.commit()
    return result.rowcount


# ---------- the team's view ----------

def summary(session: Session, settings: Settings, recent: int = 10) -> dict:
    """Counts by status and the last errors: no bodies, no addresses, no customer data."""
    counts = dict(session.exec(select(Outbox.status, func.count()).group_by(Outbox.status)).all())
    errors = session.exec(select(Outbox).where(Outbox.last_error != "").order_by(Outbox.updated_at.desc())
                          .limit(recent)).all()
    return {"counts": {k: counts.get(k, 0) for k in ("queued", "sending", "sent", "failed", "dead")},
            "sent_today": sent_today(session), "daily_limit": settings.smtp_daily_limit,
            "recent_errors": [{"id": r.id, "kind": r.kind, "status": r.status, "attempts": r.attempts,
                               "error": r.last_error, "at": aware(r.updated_at).isoformat()} for r in errors]}


def dead_recently(session: Session, days: int = 1) -> int:
    return session.exec(select(func.count()).select_from(Outbox).where(
        Outbox.status == "dead", Outbox.updated_at >= utcnow() - timedelta(days=days),
        ~Outbox.last_error.startswith("expired"))).one()

    """Startup: mail left `sending` by a crash is queued again (same Message-ID)."""
    now = utcnow()
    result = session.exec(update(Outbox).where(Outbox.status == "sending").values(  # type: ignore[call-overload]

    session.commit()

    return {"counts": {k: counts.get(k, 0) for k in ("queued", "sending", "sent", "failed", "dead")},

def dead_recently(session: Session, days: int = 1) -> int:

        Outbox.status == "dead", Outbox.updated_at >= utcnow() - timedelta(days=days),
        ~Outbox.last_error.startswith("expired"))).one()

def test_contact_mail_failure_is_a_plain_error(client, mailer, engine):
    def boom(**_kw):
        raise OSError("smtp down")

    mailer.send = boom
    r = client.post("/api/contact", json=FORM)
    assert r.status_code == 503 and "couldn't send" in r.json()["detail"]
    with Session(engine) as s:
        assert s.exec(select(AuditEvent).where(AuditEvent.action == "contact_form")).one().result == "failed"

    class DownMailer:
        def send(self, **_kw):

"""Team (admin) pages: approval queue, users, shops, reports. Every action is written to the audit log."""

import logging
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app import accounts, audit
from app.config import Settings, get_settings
from app.db import get_session
from app.integrations import Integrations, get_integrations
from app.mail.smtp import Mailer, get_mailer
from app.models import Business, Membership, ShopReport, User
from app.safety.access import Actor, require_admin
from app.sites.hosts import is_public, site_url

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/admin", tags=["admin"])
AdminDep = Annotated[Actor, Depends(require_admin)]


def iso(v) -> str | None:
    return v.replace(tzinfo=None).isoformat() + "Z" if v else None


def user_out(session: Session, u: User) -> dict:
    shops = session.exec(select(Business.name).join(Membership, Membership.business_id == Business.id)
                         .where(Membership.user_id == u.id)).all()
    return {"id": u.id, "email": u.email, "status": u.status, "role": u.role, "status_reason": u.status_reason,
            "created_at": iso(u.created_at), "last_login_at": iso(u.last_login_at), "shops": list(shops)}


def tell(mailer: Mailer, session: Session, user: User, subject: str, body: str) -> bool:
    """Email the user about a decision. A mail failure never undoes the decision; it is logged."""
    try:
        mailer.send(to=user.email, subject=subject, body=body + "\n\n- LaunchWitness")
        return True
    except Exception as e:
        log.warning("could not email a decision: %s", type(e).__name__)
        audit.record(session, actor="system", action="decision_email", target=f"user:{user.id}", result="failed",
                     detail=type(e).__name__)
        return False

def _suspend(session: Session, u: User, reason: str) -> int:
    u.status, u.status_reason = "suspended", reason.strip()
    session.add(u)
    paused = 0
    for b in session.exec(select(Business).join(Membership, Membership.business_id == Business.id)
                          .where(Membership.user_id == u.id)).all():
        if not b.paused:

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_app: FastAPI):
    from app import singleton

    # ONE process only: the scheduler runs in-process and SQLite has one writer. A second worker
    # would send every alert and daily test order twice, so it refuses to start.
    singleton.acquire(get_settings().database_url)
    init_db()
    from app.db import get_engine
    from app.startup import reconcile

    closed = reconcile(get_engine())  # close launches / check runs that lost their worker in a restart
    logging.getLogger("launchwitness").warning("startup reconcile: %s", closed)
    settings = get_settings()
    from app.accounts import ensure_admin
    from app.integrations import get_practice_integrations
    from app.tenancy import purge_old_guest_shops

    ensure_admin(get_engine(), settings)  # the ADMIN_EMAIL account exists and is the admin
    from app.selfcheck import warnings

    for w in warnings(settings):  # startup self-check: wrong-for-production settings, never a secret
        logging.getLogger("launchwitness").warning("self-check [%s]: %s", w.code, w.text)
    purge_old_guest_shops(get_engine(), settings, get_practice_integrations())
    monitor = start_monitor(settings) if settings.monitor_enabled else None
    yield
    if monitor is not None:
        monitor.shutdown()

    app = FastAPI(title="LaunchWitness", lifespan=lifespan if run_lifespan else None,
