Retry + backoff, dead letters, idempotency, a crash mid-send, the daily budget and priorities, an expired link, an order kept when the mail server is down, and no double send.""" import json import smtplib import threading import time from datetime import timedelta import pytest from sqlmodel import Session, select from app import outbox from app.db import init_db, make_engine from app.models import AuditEvent, Order, Outbox, utcnow from app.startup import reconcile from tests.conftest import ADMIN_TOKEN from tests.test_s9_phase1 import HOST, ORDER, launched_shop ADMIN = {"X-Admin-Token": ADMIN_TOKEN} def put(session, settings, mailer, key="k1", kind="alert", channel="smtp", **kw): return outbox.send(session, settings, mailer, kind=kind, key=key, to="owner@example.org", subject="Hello", body="Body", channel=channel, **kw) def rows(engine) -> list[Outbox]: with Session(engine) as s: return list(s.exec(select(Outbox).order_by(Outbox.id)).all()) def later(seconds: float): return utcnow() + timedelta(seconds=seconds) # ---------- retry, backoff, dead letters ---------- def test_temporary_failure_is_retried_with_growing_waits_then_sent(engine, settings, mailer): mailer.fail = True with Session(engine) as s: row = put(s, settings, mailer) assert row.status == "failed" and row.attempts == 1 and row.last_error == "ConnectionError" first_wait = (outbox.aware(row.next_try_at) - utcnow()).total_seconds() assert 0.8 * outbox.BASE_DELAY_S - 2 <= first_wait <= 1.2 * outbox.BASE_DELAY_S assert outbox.run_once(engine, settings, lambda _c: mailer) == {} # not due yet: nothing tried assert outbox.run_once(engine, settings, lambda _c: mailer, now=later(40)) == {"failed": 1} second = rows(engine)[0] assert second.attempts == 2 assert (outbox.aware(second.next_try_at) - utcnow()).total_seconds() > first_wait # waits longer each time mailer.fail = False assert outbox.run_once(engine, settings, lambda _c: mailer, now=later(200)) == {"sent": 1} done = rows(engine)[0] assert done.status == "sent" and done.message_id and done.last_error == "" and len(mailer.sent) == 1 def test_backoff_doubles_with_jitter_and_is_capped(): for n in range(1, 15): base = min(outbox.MAX_DELAY_S, outbox.BASE_DELAY_S * 2 ** (n - 1)) got = [outbox.backoff(n) for _ in range(30)] assert all(0.8 * base <= g <= 1.2 * base for g in got) assert len({round(g, 3) for g in got}) > 1 # jitter: not all at the same moment def test_permanent_refusal_is_dead_at_once_and_the_team_is_warned(client, engine, settings, mailer): def refuse(**_kw): raise smtplib.SMTPRecipientsRefused({"owner@example.org": (550, b"no such user owner@example.org")}) mailer.send = refuse with Session(engine) as s: row = put(s, settings, mailer) assert row.status == "dead" and row.attempts == 1 assert row.last_error == "SMTPRecipientsRefused 550" and "@" not in row.last_error # no address kept assert "outbox_dead" in client.get("/api/health", headers=ADMIN).json().get("warning_codes", []) assert "outbox_dead" not in client.get("/api/health").json().get("warning_codes", []) # the team only assert outbox.run_once(engine, settings, lambda _c: mailer, now=later(3600)) == {} # never tried again def test_a_refused_mail_sign_in_is_not_permanent(engine, settings, mailer): def bad_password(**_kw): raise smtplib.SMTPAuthenticationError(535, b"auth failed") mailer.send = bad_password with Session(engine) as s: assert put(s, settings, mailer).status == "failed" # the team can fix the password: keep trying def test_too_many_temporary_failures_end_dead(engine, settings, mailer): mailer.fail = True with Session(engine) as s: put(s, settings, mailer) for i in range(outbox.MAX_ATTEMPTS + 2): outbox.run_once(engine, settings, lambda _c: mailer, now=later(4000 * (i + 1))) row = rows(engine)[0] assert row.status == "dead" and row.attempts == outbox.MAX_ATTEMPTS # ---------- idempotency, crash, two senders ---------- def test_the_same_key_is_saved_and_sent_once(engine, settings, mailer): with Session(engine) as s: a = put(s, settings, mailer, key="order:1") b = put(s, settings, mailer, key="order:1", retry_now=True) assert a.id == b.id and len(rows(engine)) == 1 and len(mailer.sent) == 1 def test_a_crash_mid_send_is_requeued_with_the_same_message_id(engine, settings, mailer): with Session(engine) as s: row, _ = outbox.enqueue(s, settings, kind="alert", key="k", to="o@example.org", subject="s", body="b") planned = json.loads(row.ref_json)["planned_id"] assert outbox.claim(s, row.id, utcnow()) # the process dies here, between "sending" and the answer assert rows(engine)[0].status == "sending" assert outbox.run_once(engine, settings, lambda _c: mailer) == {} # a fresh claim isn't stolen assert reconcile(engine)["outbox"] == 1 # the restart puts it back in the queue assert rows(engine)[0].status == "failed" and "restarted" in rows(engine)[0].last_error seen = [] mailer_send = mailer.send def spy(**kw): seen.append(kw.get("message_id")) return mailer_send(**kw) mailer.send = spy assert outbox.run_once(engine, settings, lambda _c: mailer) == {"sent": 1} assert seen == [planned] # same Message-ID, so a copy sent just before the crash shows as one email def test_a_stale_claim_is_freed_by_the_sender_job(engine, settings, mailer): with Session(engine) as s: row, _ = outbox.enqueue(s, settings, kind="alert", key="k", to="o@example.org", subject="s", body="b") outbox.claim(s, row.id, utcnow() - timedelta(minutes=11)) got = outbox.run_once(engine, settings, lambda _c: mailer) assert got == {"reclaimed": 1, "sent": 1} and len(mailer.sent) == 1 def test_two_senders_never_send_the_same_email_twice(tmp_path, settings): engine = make_engine(f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'two.db'}") init_db(engine) sent, gate = [], threading.Barrier(2) class Slow: def send(self, **kw): sent.append(kw["to"]) time.sleep(0.2) return "" with Session(engine) as s: for i in range(5): outbox.enqueue(s, settings, kind="alert", key=f"k{i}", to=f"o{i}@example.org", subject="s", body="b") def worker(): gate.wait() outbox.run_once(engine, settings, lambda _c: Slow()) threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker) for _ in range(2)] for t in threads: t.start() for t in threads: t.join() assert sorted(sent) == sorted(f"o{i}@example.org" for i in range(5)) # each exactly once with Session(engine) as s: assert all(r.status == "sent" for r in s.exec(select(Outbox)).all()) row = s.exec(select(Outbox)).first() assert not outbox.claim(s, row.id, utcnow(), ignore_backoff=True) # a sent row can't be claimed again # ---------- budget and priorities ---------- def fill_today(engine, n: int) -> None: with Session(engine) as s: for i in range(n): s.add(Outbox(key=f"old{i}", kind="alert", to_addr="x@example.org", subject="s", status="sent", sent_at=utcnow(), channel="smtp")) s.commit() @pytest.mark.parametrize("used, held", [(3, set()), (4, {"test_order", "digest"}), (5, {"test_order", "digest", "alert", "team"})]) def test_near_the_daily_budget_low_priority_mail_waits_and_sign_ins_and_orders_never_do( make_settings, engine, mailer, used, held): settings = make_settings(smtp_daily_limit=5) fill_today(engine, used) with Session(engine) as s: for kind in ("login", "order", "alert", "team", "test_order", "digest"): row = put(s, settings, mailer, key=f"new-{kind}", kind=kind) assert (row.status == "queued") == (kind in held), kind if kind in held: assert row.last_error == "waiting: daily send budget" and row.attempts == 0 # reset so the next kinds see the same count else: s.delete(row) s.commit() s.exec(select(Outbox)).all() fill = s.exec(select(Outbox).where(Outbox.status == "sent", Outbox.key.startswith("new-"))).all() assert fill == [] def test_practice_mail_doesnt_use_the_real_budget(make_settings, engine, mailer): settings = make_settings(smtp_daily_limit=1) fill_today(engine, 1) with Session(engine) as s: assert put(s, settings, mailer, kind="digest", channel="practice").status == "sent" assert put(s, settings, mailer, key="k2", kind="digest").status == "queued" def test_held_mail_goes_out_the_next_day(make_settings, engine, mailer): settings = make_settings(smtp_daily_limit=1) fill_today(engine, 1) with Session(engine) as s: put(s, settings, mailer, kind="digest") tomorrow = outbox.start_of_day(utcnow()) + timedelta(days=1, minutes=1) assert outbox.run_once(engine, settings, lambda _c: mailer, now=tomorrow) == {"sent": 1} # ---------- sign-in links ---------- def test_a_link_that_would_arrive_expired_is_dropped_and_forgotten(engine, settings, mailer): mailer.fail = True with Session(engine) as s: row = put(s, settings, mailer, key="login:x", kind="login", html="link", expires_at=utcnow() + timedelta(minutes=13)) assert row.status == "failed" mailer.fail = False assert outbox.run_once(engine, settings, lambda _c: mailer, now=later(14 * 60)) == {"dead": 1} row = rows(engine)[0] assert mailer.sent == [] and row.body == "" and row.html == "" and row.last_error.startswith("expired") def test_a_sign_in_link_is_kept_retried_and_then_forgotten_once_sent(make_settings, engine, claude, integ): from tests.test_s9_phase2_access import AppClient, make_app integ.mailer.fail = True app, settings = make_app(make_settings, engine, integ.mailer, claude, integ, dev_mode=False) with AppClient(app) as c: r = c.post("/api/auth/request-link", json={"email": "m@example.org"}) assert r.status_code == 200 and r.json()["mail_delayed"] is True row = rows(engine)[0] assert row.kind == "login" and row.priority == 0 and row.status == "failed" assert outbox.aware(row.expires_at) <= utcnow() + timedelta(minutes=13, seconds=5) # 15 min link, 2 min margin integ.mailer.fail = False assert outbox.run_once(engine, settings, lambda _c: integ.mailer, now=later(60)) == {"sent": 1} row = rows(engine)[0] assert "signin/confirm" in integ.mailer.sent[-1]["body"] and row.body == "" and row.html == "" # ---------- orders ---------- def test_an_order_is_kept_when_the_mail_server_is_down_and_sent_later(client, engine, settings, integ): biz, _p = launched_shop(client, engine, owner_email="meera@example.org") integ.mailer.fail = True r = client.post("/order", data=ORDER, headers=HOST) assert r.status_code == 200 and "Thank you" in r.text # the customer's order went through listed = client.get(f"/api/businesses/{biz['id']}/orders").json()["orders"] assert listed[0]["email_status"] == "retrying" with Session(engine) as s: order = s.exec(select(Order).where(Order.is_test == False)).one() # if when.tzinfo is None:
        when = when.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
    return (when - datetime.now(UTC)).days


def expiry_info(ctx: Ctx) -> dict:
    info: dict = {"cert_days_left": None, "domain_days_left": None, "app_domain_days_left": None}
    try:
        info["cert_days_left"] = days_left(ctx.integ.http.cert_expires(ctx.plan.site_host))
        if ctx.plan.mode == "full":  # the seller's own name: the seller renews (and pays)
            info["domain_days_left"] = days_left(ctx.integ.godaddy.domain_expires(ctx.plan.zone))
        else:  # sandbox addresses live under the app's own domain: the team renews it (Renewals card)
            info["app_domain_days_left"] = days_left(ctx.integ.godaddy.domain_expires(ctx.settings.app_domain))
    except Exception as e:  # informational only; never breaks a check run
        info["error"] = type(e).__name__
    return info


def run_checks(engine: Engine, settings: Settings, integ: Integrations, claude: Claude, plan_id: int, *,
               trigger: str, names: list[str] | None = None, fix: bool = True, run_id: int | None = None,
               symptom: str = "", budget_seconds: float | None = None) -> RunSummary:
    """`symptom`: the owner's own words about what's wrong (optional). Data for the Doctor, never instructions.
    `budget_seconds`: once this much time is used, the remaining checks are recorded as "couldn't finish"
    (never as passed), so one slow shop can't hold up a monitoring round."""
    started = clock()
    with Session(engine) as session:
        plan = session.get(Plan, plan_id)
        business = session.get(Business, plan.business_id)
        if plan.status != "done":
            raise NotLaunched(plan_id)
        run = session.get(CheckRun, run_id) if run_id else None
        if run is None:
            run = start_run(session, business.id, plan.id, trigger)  # raises AlreadyChecking
        ctx = Ctx(session, settings, integ, plan, business, run_id=run.id)
        outs: list[Outcome] = []
        try:
            apply_demo_fault(ctx)
            repairs, failed = [], []
            for name in names or checks_for(ctx):  # check, and repair right away, so later checks see the fix
                if budget_seconds is not None and clock() - started > budget_seconds:
                    out = Outcome(name, False, OUT_OF_TIME, f"time budget of {budget_seconds:.0f}s used up",
                                  unfinished=True)
                    save(session, ctx, out, 0)
                    outs.append(out)
                    failed.append(out)
                    continue
                out = run_check(ctx, name)
                outs.append(out)
                if out.passed:
                    continue
                if out.unfinished:  # we don't know: nothing to fix, nobody to blame
                    failed.append(out)
                    continue
                fixable = fixes_for(out.check, plan.mode) or needs_a_look(out)
                done = fixes_today(session, business.id, out.check) if fix and fixable else 0
                if done >= MAX_AUTO_FIXES_PER_DAY:  # flapping: stop the fix loop, hand it to the owner
                    out.keeps_breaking = True
                    repairs.append({"check": out.check, "fixed": False, "attempts": [], "keeps_breaking": True,
                                    "doctor": needs_you(
                        ctx, out.check, "This keeps breaking, so we've stopped fixing it automatically.",
                        KEEPS_BREAKING.format(n=done))})
                elif not fixable:  # no automatic fix exists: the owner still gets exact plain steps
                    repairs.append({"check": out.check, "fixed": False, "attempts": [], "doctor": needs_you(
                        ctx, out.check, out.plain, next_step(out.check, plan.mode, out.plain))})
                elif fix:
                    r = repair(claude, ctx, out, symptom)
                    repairs.append({"check": r.check, "fixed": r.fixed, "attempts": r.attempts,
                                    **({"doctor": r.doctor} if r.doctor else {})})
                    if r.fixed:
                        continue
                    out = r.final or out
                failed.append(out)
            info = expiry_info(ctx)
        except Exception as e:  # keep the run row consistent; report shows it as not passed
            audit.record(session, actor="checker", action="check_run", target=f"run:{run.id}", result="failed",
                         business_id=business.id, detail=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:300])
            failed, repairs, info = [Outcome("check_run", False, "We couldn't finish the checks.", str(e))], [], {}
        run.status, run.passed, run.finished_at = "done", not failed, utcnow()
        run.repairs_json, run.info_json = json.dumps(repairs), json.dumps(info)
        session.add(run)
        session.commit()
        audit.record(session, actor="checker", action="check_run", target=f"run:{run.id}",
                     result="pass" if not failed else "fail", business_id=business.id,
                     detail=f"{trigger}: {len(outs)} checks, "
                            f"{len(repairs)} repaired/attempted, failing: {[f.check for f in failed]}")
        return RunSummary(run.id, not failed, failed)

"""One-off: measure today's monitoring rounds on the 40-shop slow world (run with pytest)."""
import time

import pytest

from app.monitor.scheduler import Monitor
from tests.scale_world import SlowWorld, build_shops, projected


@pytest.fixture
def settings(make_settings, tmp_path):
    return make_settings(database_url=f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'scale.db'}")


def test_measure_today(client, engine, settings, integ, claude):
    build_shops(client, engine)
    world = SlowWorld(integ)
    mon = Monitor(engine, settings, lambda _b: integ, claude)
    for kind in ("quick", "daily"):
        t = time.monotonic()
        getattr(mon, f"run_{kind}")()
        real = time.monotonic() - t
        print(f"\nTODAY {kind}: {real:.2f}s real = {projected(real):.0f}s simulated; godaddy max/min {world.most_godaddy_calls_in_a_minute()}; max parallel calls {world.max_busy}")
    world.release.set()
EOF

"""S13 B: one shared limit on GoDaddy API calls for the whole process (GoDaddy allows 60 requests a minute per
endpoint; we stay under that across ALL endpoints, so monitoring many shops at once can't get us blocked).

A sliding window: at most `calls` in any `period` seconds. A caller over the limit waits (it never fails).
"""

import threading
import time
from collections import deque
from collections.abc import Callable

GODADDY_PER_MINUTE = 50


class RateLimiter:
    def __init__(self, calls: int = GODADDY_PER_MINUTE, period: float = 60.0,
                 clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic, sleep: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep):
        self.calls, self.period, self.clock, self.sleep = calls, period, clock, sleep
        self._times: deque[float] = deque()
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self.waited = 0.0  # total seconds callers waited (for the team's numbers and tests)

    def acquire(self) -> None:
        while True:
            with self._lock:
                now = self.clock()
                while self._times and self._times[0] <= now - self.period:
                    self._times.popleft()
                if len(self._times) < self.calls:
                    self._times.append(now)
                    return
                wait = self._times[0] + self.period - now
            self.waited += max(wait, 0.0)
            self.sleep(max(wait, 0.001))


LIMITER = RateLimiter()  # every real GoDaddy request in this process goes through this one

"""S13 B: monitoring at the 40-shop scale, on the slow pretend world (`tests/scale_world.py`, times scaled 50x).

Measured BEFORE this change (one shop after another): quick round 534 s, daily round 670 s (simulated), the
hanging shop holding every shop behind it. The numbers after are printed by `test_40_shops_finish_well_inside…`.
"""

import json
import threading
import time

import pytest
from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app import chain
from app.godaddy.ratelimit import RateLimiter
from app.models import Alert, AuditEvent, Business, CheckResult, CheckRun, Evidence
from app.monitor.scheduler import (
    CHECK_WATCHDOG,
    DAILY_SLOTS,
    QUICK_MINUTES,
    ROUND_DEADLINE,
    SHOP_BUDGET,
    Monitor,
)
from tests.scale_world import FAIL, HANG, N_SHOPS, SCALE, SLOW, SlowWorld, build_shops, projected

pytestmark = pytest.mark.filterwarnings("ignore::pytest.PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning")


@pytest.fixture
def settings(make_settings, tmp_path):
    # a file database: shops really run side by side (the in-memory test DB is one shared connection)
    return make_settings(database_url=f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'scale.db'}", max_shops_per_user=100,
                         user_describes_per_day=100, monitor_workers=4)


def scaled_monitor(engine, settings, integ, claude) -> Monitor:
    m = Monitor(engine, settings, lambda _b: integ, claude)
    m.budgets = {k: v * SCALE for k, v in SHOP_BUDGET.items()}
    m.check_seconds = CHECK_WATCHDOG * SCALE
    m.round_deadline = {k: v * SCALE for k, v in ROUND_DEADLINE.items()}
    m.inbox_pass_seconds = 60 * SCALE
    return m


@pytest.fixture
def world(client, engine, settings, integ, claude):
    shops = build_shops(client, engine)
    slow = SlowWorld(integ)
    yield shops, slow, scaled_monitor(engine, settings, integ, claude)
    slow.release.set()  # let the hanging call return so its thread ends


def ids_by_name(engine) -> dict[str, int]:
    with Session(engine) as s:
        return {b.subdomain: b.id for b in s.exec(select(Business)).all()}


def results(engine, bid: int, check: str) -> list[dict]:
    with Session(engine) as s:
        rows = s.exec(select(CheckResult).join(CheckRun, CheckRun.id == CheckResult.run_id).where(
            CheckResult.business_id == bid, CheckResult.check == check, CheckRun.trigger.like("monitor_%"))).all()
        return [json.loads(r.detail) | {"passed": r.passed} for r in rows]


def test_40_shops_finish_well_inside_15_minutes_and_the_hanging_one_delays_nobody(world, engine):
    _shops, slow, mon = world
    names = ids_by_name(engine)
    times = {}
    for kind in ("quick", "daily"):
        started = time.monotonic()
        got = mon._round(kind)
        times[kind] = projected(time.monotonic() - started)
        assert got["checked"] == N_SHOPS and got["unfinished"] == [] and got["busy"] == [], got
    print(f"\nAFTER (simulated s, 4 workers): quick {times['quick']:.0f}, daily {times['daily']:.0f}; "
          f"most calls in flight at once {slow.max_busy}")
    assert times["quick"] < 5 * 60 and times["daily"] < 5 * 60  # was 534 s and 670 s; the limit is 15 minutes
    assert slow.max_busy > 1  # really side by side
    # the hanging shop: its page check is "couldn't finish" (never passed), and it's said why
    hang = results(engine, names[HANG], "https")
    assert hang and all(not r["passed"] and r.get("unfinished") for r in hang)
    assert all("stopped waiting" in r["detail"] for r in hang)
    # ...and it delayed nobody: every ordinary shop finished long before the watchdog gave up on it
    with Session(engine) as s:
        quick = s.exec(select(CheckRun).where(CheckRun.trigger == "monitor_quick")).all()
    start = min(proof_time(r.started_at) for r in quick)
    ordinary = [r for r in quick if r.business_id not in {names[HANG], names[FAIL]}]
    latest = max(proof_time(r.finished_at) for r in ordinary)
    assert projected((latest - start).total_seconds()) < CHECK_WATCHDOG * 0.7
    slow_ones = {names[n] for n in SLOW}
    assert all(r.passed for r in ordinary if r.business_id not in slow_ones) and all(
        r.passed for r in ordinary if r.business_id in slow_ones)  # slow is never called broken


def proof_time(when):
    from app.monitor.scheduler import proof_aware

    return proof_aware(when)


def test_alert_rules_still_hold_at_scale(world, engine):
    _shops, _slow, mon = world
    names = ids_by_name(engine)
    mon._round("quick")
    jobs = {j.id for j in mon.scheduler.get_jobs()}
    assert f"recheck-{names[FAIL]}" in jobs  # a real failure is re-checked a minute later
    assert f"recheck-{names[HANG]}" not in jobs  # "couldn't finish" is not a failure: no re-check, no alert
    assert len([j for j in jobs if j.startswith("recheck-")]) == 1
    with Session(engine) as s:
        assert s.exec(select(Alert)).all() == []  # nothing is emailed from the first look


def test_no_round_stacks_on_another_and_a_busy_shop_is_skipped(world, engine):
    _shops, slow, mon = world
    names = ids_by_name(engine)
    mon.check_seconds = 10_000  # no watchdog: the hanging shop stays busy past the round's deadline
    mon.round_deadline = {"quick": 30 * SCALE, "daily": 30 * SCALE}
    got = {}
    t = threading.Thread(target=lambda: got.setdefault("first", mon._round("quick")))
    t.start()
    time.sleep(5 * SCALE)
    assert mon._round("quick") == {"skipped_round": True}  # a second round never stacks
    t.join()
    assert got["first"]["unfinished"] == [names[HANG]]  # reported, and the round didn't wait for it
    again = mon._round("quick")  # the next round: the hanging shop's previous check is still running
    assert again["busy"] == [names[HANG]] and names[HANG] not in range(0)  # skipped, not run twice
    with Session(engine) as s:
        rows = s.exec(select(AuditEvent).where(AuditEvent.action.in_(("monitor_round", "monitor_shop")))).all()
    assert {r.result for r in rows} >= {"skipped", "unfinished"}
    slow.release.set()


def test_godaddy_calls_stay_under_the_rate_limit(world, integ):
    _shops, slow, mon = world
    integ.godaddy.limiter = RateLimiter(calls=10, period=60 * SCALE)  # stricter than ours, to see it bite
    mon._round("daily")
    assert slow.most_godaddy_calls_in_a_minute() <= 10
    assert integ.godaddy.limiter.waited > 0  # the limit really held calls back (40 shops read the zone)


def test_the_evidence_chain_stays_intact_under_concurrency(world, engine):
    _shops, _slow, mon = world
    mon._round("daily")
    mon._round("quick")
    with Session(engine) as s:
        ids = [b.id for b in s.exec(select(Business)).all()]
        total = 0
        for bid in ids:
            v = chain.verify(s, bid)
            assert v["intact"], (bid, v)
            total += v["rows"]
        assert total == len(s.exec(select(Evidence)).all()) and total > N_SHOPS * 3


def test_slots_spread_the_shops_over_15_minutes_and_the_day():
    ids = list(range(1, N_SHOPS + 1))
    per_minute = [sum(1 for b in ids if Monitor.slot(b, QUICK_MINUTES) == m) for m in range(QUICK_MINUTES)]
    assert sum(per_minute) == N_SHOPS and max(per_minute) <= 6  # 40 shops: 2-3 a minute, never all at once
    assert Monitor.slot(7, QUICK_MINUTES) == Monitor.slot(7, QUICK_MINUTES)  # stable
    daily = {Monitor.slot(b, DAILY_SLOTS) for b in ids}
    assert len(daily) >= N_SHOPS - 2  # nearly every shop its own minute of the day


def test_each_tick_checks_only_the_shops_whose_slot_it_is_plus_the_overdue(world, engine):
    from datetime import timedelta

@pytest.fixture
def settings(make_settings, tmp_path):

                         user_describes_per_day=100, monitor_workers=4)


def scaled_monitor(engine, settings, integ, claude) -> Monitor:
    m = Monitor(engine, settings, lambda _b: integ, claude)
    m.budgets = {k: v * SCALE for k, v in SHOP_BUDGET.items()}
    m.check_seconds = CHECK_WATCHDOG * SCALE
    m.round_deadline = {k: v * SCALE for k, v in ROUND_DEADLINE.items()}
    m.inbox_pass_seconds = 60 * SCALE
    return m

    with Session(engine) as s:

            CheckResult.business_id == bid, CheckResult.check == check, CheckRun.trigger.like("monitor_%"))).all()
        return [json.loads(r.detail) | {"passed": r.passed} for r in rows]

    names = ids_by_name(engine)

    slow_ones = {names[n] for n in SLOW}
    assert all(r.passed for r in ordinary if r.business_id not in slow_ones) and all(
        r.passed for r in ordinary if r.business_id in slow_ones)  # slow is never called broken

    return proof_aware(when)

    assert n == 1
    integ.inbox.deliver(sender="hello@example.com", to="meera@example.org", subject=f"[TEST] {item['nonce']}",

        assert len(seen) == 1 and seen[0].nonce == item["nonce"]
        assert chain.verify(s, bid)["intact"]

    assert f"recheck-{bid}" in {j.id for j in mon.scheduler.get_jobs()}  # the usual re-check + Doctor + alert path

content.content:
## 7. Monitoring after launch

Light monitoring is core; full only if time permits. It re-runs launch checks on a timer (GoDaddy's API has no webhooks).

**Light (build now)**

| How often | What |
|---|---|
| Every 15 minutes | Site opens, HTTPS valid |
| Daily | DNS + email settings still match launch; days left on certificate and domain |

- On failure: re-check once a minute later (rule out blips), then Doctor explains + safe playbook fix.
- Anything needing money or her action (renewal, payment): alert only, at 30 / 7 / 1 days before expiry.
- Alerts go to her **personal email**, not the business inbox.
- "Run checks now" button = same checks on demand (this is how the demo shows it).

**Full (if time permits):** daily real test order; change detection ("Was this you? Tap to restore") instead of silent undo; incident history on the report.

**Rules every check and alert follows (S11b; the full table of cases is `docs/CHECKS_MATRIX.md`)**

- Each finding says how sure we are: seen / not seen / couldn't check. "Not sure" is allowed; a wrong answer is not.
- A lookup that fails on our side is "couldn't check": never passed, never the seller's fault, no fix, no alert.
- The email service is detected from the domain's own mail servers. Advice only ever uses that service's values; an unrecognised service gets no values. A signing key is "found" or "couldn't check", never "missing".
- Outside addresses (Check any address, Watch) are explained only. Fixes exist only for our own shops, and never touch another email service's working settings.
- Each shop has a time budget per round; what didn't finish is recorded as "couldn't finish".
- A check fixed 3 times in a day that breaks again is no longer fixed automatically: one "keeps breaking" email, then it needs the owner.
- An alert that couldn't be sent is recorded, retried on the next round, and shown to the team.

**Honest framing:** in the demo everything sits in the app's GoDaddy account, so little can break after launch. Monitoring matters most once it runs on her own account. Pitch it as insurance, not the hero.

---

state='''## Session 13 (Opus, 2026-11-17, laptop): live S12 fixtures, the email outbox, monitoring at 40 shops (STOPPED EARLY)

Branch `s13-reliability`, each part merged into **main** with `--no-ff` and pushed. **Stopped by the owner after Part B**:
Part C (weekly digest + public resolvers) and the final Docker/e2e verification were NOT done. Pick up below.

Done:
- **Part 0** (`ca4ea5e`): the 11 S12 Doctor placeholders captured live (14 Haiku calls, **$0.0025**; cap $0.10).
  `REQUIRE_LIVE_FIXTURES=1 pytest tests/test_s6_agents.py tests/test_s11c_live.py` passes. Script fixes: an `evidence`
  answer for `https_marker_symptom` (the live model asked for it and the script crashed) and `--only key,key`.
  `test_s12_ui` now compares with the saved symptom fixture (it had checked the placeholder's "You said" wording).
  Also: the laptop venv lacked Pillow (S12): `pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt`.
- **Part A** (`3bd4397`): `app/outbox.py` + `Outbox` table. Every email (sign-in, orders, test orders, alerts, team
  renewals, watch, contact, shop reports, admin decisions) is saved under a unique key, tried at once (5 s sign-in,
  10 s order), then retried by the sender job (`outbox_send`, every 20 s, in the monitor scheduler; its own small
  scheduler when `MONITOR_ENABLED=false`). Backoff 30 s doubling to 30 min with ±20% jitter, 10 tries (~2 h), then
  `dead` → team health `outbox_dead` + admin "Email outbox" card (`GET /api/admin/outbox`: counts + error kinds, no
  bodies/addresses). Permanent = 5xx refusal / bad address; a refused mail sign-in (535) is NOT permanent. Atomic claim
  (one UPDATE), stale `sending` > 10 min freed, startup reconcile requeues `sending` (same planned Message-ID).
  Priorities 0 sign-in+orders (never held) / 1 alerts+team / 2 test orders+digest; `SMTP_DAILY_LIMIT=250` is a
  **placeholder**: priority 2 waits from 80%, priority 1 at 100%; practice mail doesn't count. Sign-in failure answers
  200 `mail_delayed: true` + "We're having trouble sending email right now. We'll keep trying…" (never "sent"); link
  rows expire 2 min before the link; their bodies are emptied once sent/dropped. Orders: saved first;
  `Order.email_status` = queued | sent | retrying | failed (Orders page: "Email to you: …"). Test-order evidence
  `smtp_accepted` uses the outbox row's Message-ID, `answer="outbox N, try K"`; a test order held by the budget is
  "couldn't finish", not failed. S11b alert retry now rides on the outbox (its tests unchanged and passing).
  `PUT /api/admin/practice-mail {"down": bool}`: team-only, pretend mail server only (for the planned e2e flow).
  Contact form: message kept; answers "We have your message. Our email is slow…" when not sent at once.
- **Part B** (this merge): `Monitor` runs shops in a pool (`MONITOR_WORKERS=4`), a one-minute beat `monitor_tick`
  (replaces `monitor_quick`/`monitor_daily`) with a stable crc32 slot per shop over 15 min and over the day, plus
  overdue catch-up (quick > 20 min, daily > 25 h). Never two rounds at once, never one shop twice (busy set); a beat
  waits ≤ 48 s. Per-check watchdog 150 s (`checker.run_check_watched`: own thread + own Session + copied rows; an
  abandoned check can't write proof). The daily test order no longer sleeps for the inbox: "accepted" now, up to 3
  one-minute `inbox_pass` looks (found → `imap_seen` through `proof.add`; still missing → row failed + the usual
  recheck). One shared GoDaddy limiter, 50 calls/min (`app/godaddy/ratelimit.py`). Measured on 40 slow fake shops
  (`tests/scale_world.py`, `tests/test_s13_scale.py`, times scaled 50×): **quick 534 s → ~163 s, daily 670 s → ~300 s**.
  Capacity note in SPEC §7: the checks would keep up with 1,000+ shops; the real limit is the mailbox's daily send
  limit (one test order per shop per day → about 0.8 × `SMTP_DAILY_LIMIT` shops).

Tests: **1036+ passed, 2 skipped** (see BUILD_LOG for the final count); ruff, `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build` clean.
**Not run this session: Docker rebuild, `check_m1.sh --local`, e2e, screenshots.** The sign-in "delayed" screen, the
Orders "Email to you" line and the admin outbox card are unverified in a browser.

Next session, in order:
1. Rebuild the stack, `bash scripts/check_m1.sh --local`, full e2e. Add the e2e flow: team `PUT /api/admin/practice-mail
   {"down":true}` → place an order on a practice shop → Orders shows "retrying" → `{"down":false}` → within ~1 min
   (backoff 30 s + 20 s job) it shows "sent". Note: on the local stack ORDER emails go to the pretend mailbox, not
   Mailpit (only sign-in/team mail reaches Mailpit), which is why the switch exists. Optionally: stop Mailpit, ask
   for a sign-in link → the "trouble sending" screen → start Mailpit → the link arrives.
2. Part C: weekly digest via the outbox (`kind="digest"`, priority 2, signed unsubscribe route in `route_table.py`), and
   the 8.8.8.8 / 1.1.1.1 / 9.9.9.9 lookup on the daily run as evidence (+ CHECKS_MATRIX row). Brief: the S13 prompt.
3. Before the VPS: set `SMTP_DAILY_LIMIT` to GoDaddy's real limit in `.env`.

Open / doubts (one line each):
- At-least-once: a crash right after the server accepted a mail but before we saved "sent" sends it again (same Message-ID).
- Watch alerts: an older unsent watch email for the same address is marked dead ("replaced") when a newer one is queued.
- A late (abandoned) check thread keeps running until its own timeout; with 4 workers several hung calls could pile up
  threads (each bounded by its call's timeout).
- `inbox_pass` jobs live in the scheduler's memory: a restart loses pending looks (that run stays "waiting").
- Tests default to `MONITOR_WORKERS=1` (the in-memory test DB is one shared connection); the scale tests use a file DB.

'''
p='docs/STATE_FOR_NEXT_SESSION.md'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
s=s.replace('# State for the next session (written 2026-11-16 IST, end of Session 12)','# State for the next session (written 2026-11-17 IST, end of Session 13)',1)
i=s.index('## Session 12 (Opus')
s=s[:i]+state+s[i:]
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)

p='docs/PROGRESS.md'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
i=s.index('**Session 12 (Nov 16, Opus)')
s=s[:i]+'''**Session 13 (Nov 17, Opus, laptop): stopped after Part B by the owner.** Part 0: the 11 S12 Doctor fixtures captured live
($0.0025). Part A: durable email outbox (every email saved first, retried with backoff, dead letters shown to the team,
daily budget with priorities, honest sign-in "trouble sending", orders never lost, "Email to you" on the Orders page).
Part B: monitoring with a 4-worker pool, per-shop slots, a per-check watchdog, non-blocking inbox look, GoDaddy rate
limit (40 shops: quick 534 s → ~163 s). **Not done: Part C (digest + public resolvers), Docker/check_m1/e2e.** Next steps
and decisions: `docs/STATE_FOR_NEXT_SESSION.md` → Session 13.

Decisions (S13): sign-in mail failure answers 200 `mail_delayed` (was 503); order audit result words are now the
outbox's (`sent`/`failed`); a refused mail sign-in is retried, not dead; practice mail doesn't count toward
`SMTP_DAILY_LIMIT`; per-check watchdog 150 s (above the padlock check's 2-minute retry); monitor jobs are one
`monitor_tick` a minute instead of two interval jobs.

'''+s[i:]
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)

p='docs/BUILD_LOG.md'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
s=s.rstrip('\n')+'''

### Session 13 — 2026-11-17 (IST) — Live S12 fixtures, an email outbox, monitoring at 40 shops (Opus, laptop)
- Goal: reliability before the VPS day: no lost email, monitoring that scales, real Doctor fixtures.
- Asked Claude to: capture the S12 fixtures live, build a durable outbox, measure and fix monitoring for 40 shops, then a weekly digest and a public-resolvers check.
- Claude built: Part 0 (11 live fixtures, $0.0025; capture script crash on an unexpected `evidence` call fixed). Part A: `app/outbox.py` + `Outbox` table, every sender moved onto it, sender job, reconcile, budget + priorities, admin card, honest sign-in/contact wording, Orders email state, 21 tests. Part B: a 40-shop slow pretend world, measured first (quick 534 s, daily 670 s simulated, one hang holds everyone), then a worker pool, per-shop slots on a one-minute beat, per-check watchdog, later inbox look, shared GoDaddy limiter (quick ~163 s, daily ~300 s), 10 tests; SPEC capacity note.
- I changed / rejected: stopped the session after Part B (Part C and the Docker/e2e verification moved to the next session). Claude flagged up front: risk of changing every email path the day before the VPS, and that a Python "watchdog" can stop waiting for a check but can't kill it.
- Result: unit suite green, ruff/tsc/build clean; Docker, check_m1 and e2e not run this session.
- Next: Docker + e2e (with the new "order while mail is down" flow), then Part C.
'''
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s+'\n')
EOF
echo done
